published_figures.source: DoD Selected Acquisition Report, F-22, December 2010; USAF F-22 fact sheet
published_figures.figure: The report's supercruise, "Vmax/Opt Alt/Mil Power": Mach 1.76, demonstrated, at military power, 0.99, and the best altitude - flown level at every 2,000 ft from 30,000 to 50,000 ft, the fastest.
The report's acceleration, "Acceleration/.8-1.5/30K": 52.4 seconds, demonstrated, from Mach 0.8 to 1.5 at 30,000 ft, at maximum power.

The report's manoeuvrability, "max power sustained G", at 30,000 ft and Mach 0.9: 3.7 g, demonstrated - a turn rate of 7.34 degrees a second, g times the root of n squared less one, over the true airspeed, 895 ft/s. The tolerance takes in the report's objective, 3.9 g.

The fact sheet's speed, "mach two class": level at 40,000 ft at full throttle it reaches Mach 2, within the class this project reads as 1.95 to 2.35. Lockheed Martin (18 November 2002) had it cleared to Mach 2.
The fact sheet's ceiling, "above 50,000 feet": at 50,000 ft, at maximum power, it still climbs at 100 ft/min, the rate that makes a service ceiling.
published_figures.plan_speeds: The slowest, 140 kt, is 5 kt over the first that held, 135: she publishes no stall speed, so has no approach speed, and the sweep began at 120 kt; below 135 she came down 500 ft before reaching her circle. At 135 she held the orbit all four ways and, on her own yaw damper and rudder integral (her catalogue's `yaw-damper`), her sideslip in the crosswind within 0.23 degree. On 2026-10-02, before them, she held her orbit only from 220 kt and swung her sideslip 6.0 degrees either way at 230 in the crosswind, and her slowest was 255. The fastest, 360 kt, a fifth over its start speed, held all four ways.
published_figures.glide_speeds: None was found: from 140 kt, her slowest under power since 2026-10-07, to 275 it stalls before it is half way round - to 265 departing past 95 degrees of alpha, why is not found - and from 280 to 360 it is less than half way round at 1,000 ft. 255 kt, her slowest under power before, is kept, so that a copilot asks no glide of her she was not asked before; the glide tests name it.
published_figures.takeoff_speeds: Rotation: from 100 kt in 5 kt steps, the first that lifted her off within 15 kt of itself, unwrecked, inside the 3,500 m runway, and never 5 kt slower once off, was 100 kt; 105 is written, 5 kt to spare, and she leaves the ground at about 115. The climb away: asked 115 to 205 kt, at military power she was at 500 ft never slower than 216.3 kt, and faster the faster asked - she cannot be held slower - which is written rounded up. With no flap, at 61,570 lb, the weight her model flies a plan at.
published_figures.no_landing_distance: Nothing public gives its landing distance: no runway is refused it for length. It has no approach speed in any case, so nothing plans it a landing.
